content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate pancakes are thin, tender crepes made from a batter that includes cocoa powder and a touch of sugar, then topped with melted chocolate or served with a chocolate sauce. They deliver a rich chocolate flavor while keeping the light, airy texture of classic pancakes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate pancakes are a popular breakfast treat in many European countries where chocolate is considered a morning flavor.
Cocoa powder adds not only taste but also antioxidant properties to the batter.
Traditional recipes use milk, eggs, and a small amount of oil to keep the pancakes soft.
In Russia, chocolate pancakes are often served with berry or nut toppings.
Gluten‑free versions exist, using rice or buckwheat flour.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Rich in carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide a quick source of energy, useful before physical activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter supplies vitamins B1, B2, and B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with vegetable oil, the amount of saturated fat remains modest.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa or chocolate.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Overly sweet pancakes can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate pancakes are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pancakes hot, drizzled with melted chocolate, dusted with cocoa powder, and topped with berries, nuts, or whipped cream. They can also be rolled with fillings such as fruit compote or cottage cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. They can be frozen in individual portions and reheated in the microwave or on a skillet.
